title: Monday Morning Quarterback
date_line: Monday, Nov. 16, 2026 · Gambler edition · By Richard J Diskin Jr

paragraphs: Thirteen Week 10 games are final, from Thursday night at MetLife Stadium to Sunday night in Cincinnati, with a Sunday morning stop in Munich. The people holding tickets got all of it: a 54-yard field goal as time ran out against the Saints, an Under that died by half a point on a 43-yard touchdown with 4:18 left, a Titans cover that held until 1:10 to go, a field goal on fourth-and-goal at the 2 that saved an Under, a 12-yard punt that set up a Thursday night winner, and a Sunday night Under that was alive by half a point with 10 minutes left.

Graded against the opening lines, the Cover Writer went 8-5 against the spread and 3-10 on the over/under. Graded against the closing lines, the Cover Writer went 8-5 against the spread and 6-7 on the over/under.
Chargers at Ravens tonight is the last Week 10 game, and it gets graded in Tuesday's edition.

Every side is graded on the team picked and every over/under on the Over or Under called, once against the opening line and once against the closing line. A push counts as neither a hit nor a miss, and overtime points count. Picks are graded as they stood at kickoff. Sunday's game-day line refresh changed some picks before any of those games started, and the ones that mattered are noted where they happened. Each game below opens with both lines and the Cover Writer's card, rides along with the tickets through the plays and flags that swung them, then lists who called it and who missed it.

Opening line: Bengals −3.5, over/under 47.5. Closing line: Bengals −4.5, over/under 49.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Steelers and the Under, projecting Bengals 25, Steelers 22. Final: Steelers 18, Bengals 38. The Bengals won by 20, and the teams scored 56 points.

Three pickers sided with the Cover Writer on the Steelers +3.5, and The Formula was the only one in the room on the Bengals −3.5. Everybody with an over/under pick had the Under 49.5 except Follow The Money, which took the Over. In The Trenches had the Over 48.5 before Sunday's game-day line refresh and switched to the Under, and that switch is about to come up.

Cincinnati built its lead in the first half. Evan McPherson kicked a 24-yarder, a 26-yard pass interference flag on Asante Samuel Jr. set up Joe Burrow's 3-yard touchdown to Drew Sample, and Burrow found Chase Brown from 2 yards out at 5:28 of the second quarter. Chris Boswell's 45-yarder got Pittsburgh on the board, and Burrow hit Dohnte Meyers for a 15-yard touchdown just before the half. Bengals 24, Steelers 3. The Steelers tickets were down 21 at the break.

The third quarter took the last bit of hope off the side. Ja'Marr Chase caught a pass at the Pittsburgh 4 and fumbled, Jack Endries fell on it for Cincinnati, and Brown caught a 4-yard touchdown pass on the next snap. Bengals 31, Steelers 3.

That left the Under as the only live ticket for most of the room. Aaron Rodgers hit DK Metcalf for a 22-yard touchdown on fourth-and-4 at 12:16 of the fourth and found Metcalf again for two points. Bengals 31, Steelers 11, 42 points. Brown looked like he scored from the 5, replay put him down at the 1, and Samaje Perine walked in from there at 10:08. Bengals 38, Steelers 11, 49 points, half a point under the 49.5 with 10 minutes to go.

The Under didn't survive the next Pittsburgh drive. Kris Jenkins Jr. was flagged for roughing the passer at 8:18, Rodgers recovered a Zach Frazier fumble on the very next snap, and Rodgers hit Pat Freiermuth for a 27-yard touchdown at 7:19. Bengals 38, Steelers 18, 56 points. Follow The Money's Over cashed, and the Under lost by 6.5 at the close. Barrett Carter thought he had a pick-six off Mason Rudolph at 3:34, and replay took it back, which saved nobody anything.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Steelers, missed by 16.5 points at the opening Steelers +3.5 and missed by 15.5 points at the closing Steelers +4.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Under, went over by 8.5 points at the opening 47.5 and went over by 6.5 points at the closing 49.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Formula on the Bengals, covered by 16.5 points at the opening Bengals −3.5 and covered by 15.5 points at the closing Bengals −4.5; Follow The Money on the Over, went over by 8.5 points at the opening 47.5 and went over by 6.5 points at the closing 49.5.
Follow The Money passed on the side.

Opening line: Cowboys −1.5, over/under 52.5. Closing line: 49ers −3.5, over/under 55.5. The Cover Writer's card had the 49ers and the Under, projecting 49ers 30, Cowboys 23. Final: 49ers 46, Cowboys 40. The 49ers won by 6, and the teams scored 86 points.

The Cover Writer, The Formula, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches had the 49ers −4.5, and Next Man Up took the Cowboys +4.5. Everybody but In The Trenches had the Under 55.5. The line moved 5 points toward San Francisco between the open and the close, and the side still came down to the final minute.

The Under was in trouble by halftime. Dak Prescott threw touchdowns of 35 and 39 yards to George Pickens, Brock Purdy hit Deebo Samuel Sr. for an 11-yard touchdown, and Christian McCaffrey took a short pass 74 yards to the end zone at 2:26 of the second. Brandon Aubrey missed the extra point after the second Pickens touchdown. 49ers 17, Cowboys 16 at the half, 33 points.

Kaelon Black ran 25 yards for a touchdown early in the third, Aubrey hit from 52, and Samuel went 70 yards on a run at 6:59. Malik Mustapha intercepted Prescott on fourth down at the San Francisco 10. McCaffrey's 16-yard touchdown run at 11:26 of the fourth made it 49ers 38, Cowboys 19, 57 points, and the Under 55.5 was gone with more than 11 minutes left.

Then it got loud on the side. Pickens caught a 5-yard touchdown at 9:08, and the two-point pass to him fell incomplete. Ryan Flournoy caught an 11-yard touchdown on fourth-and-6 at 3:42. 49ers 38, Cowboys 32. San Francisco answered in two plays: McCaffrey caught a 66-yard touchdown at 3:23 and then caught the two-point pass. 49ers 46, Cowboys 32.

Dallas wasn't done. Prescott converted a fourth-and-1, a 14-yard pass interference flag on Ephesians Prysock put the ball at the 1, and CeeDee Lamb caught a 1-yard touchdown at 0:43. Prescott ran in the two-point try. 49ers 46, Cowboys 40, and the 49ers −4.5 was covering by 1.5. A Dallas field goal would have flipped it. Deebo Samuel Sr. fielded the onside kick, the 49ers punted Dallas back to its own 9, and the last play turned into a string of laterals that ended with Marques Sigle recovering a fumble. The 49ers −4.5 survived, and 86 points beat the Under by 30.5 at the close.

Missed at both numbers: Next Man Up on the Cowboys, missed by 7.5 points at the opening Cowboys −1.5 and missed by 2.5 points at the closing Cowboys +3.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Under, went over by 33.5 points at the opening 52.5 and went over by 30.5 points at the closing 55.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the 49ers, covered by 7.5 points at the opening 49ers +1.5 and covered by 2.5 points at the closing 49ers −3.5; In The Trenches on the Over, went over by 33.5 points at the opening 52.5 and went over by 30.5 points at the closing 55.5.
Follow The Money sat out the side and the over/under.

Opening line: Seahawks −7, over/under 43.5. Closing line: Seahawks −6.5, over/under 40.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Seahawks and the Over, projecting Seahawks 26, Raiders 19. Final: Seahawks 21, Raiders 13. The Seahawks won by 8, and the teams scored 34 points.

The Cover Writer, The Formula, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money had the Seahawks −6.5. Next Man Up and In The Trenches had the Seahawks −3.5 before Sunday's game-day line refresh and finished on the Raiders +6.5. Five pickers had the Over 40.5, and Follow The Money took the Under.

The Raiders scored first after Quay Walker recovered a sack-fumble on Seattle's second snap, and Fernando Mendoza ran 10 yards for the touchdown. Jaxon Smith-Njigba had a 29-yard touchdown wiped out by his own offensive pass interference, and Cooper Kupp caught a 34-yard touchdown on third-and-15 later in the same drive. Matt Gay's 34-yarder made it Raiders 10, Seahawks 7, and that was the half.

Jadarian Price ran 12 yards for a touchdown at 9:28 of the third. A Mendoza fumble was overturned on replay, and on the next Seattle possession Smith-Njigba got his touchdown back with a 71-yarder at 7:10. Seahawks 21, Raiders 10, 31 points.

That's where the Over died slowly. Seattle drove 14 plays and gave it away on a sack-fumble at the Raiders' 12, recovered by Nakobe Dean at 12:17 of the fourth. Jason Myers missed a 44-yarder wide right at 7:05. A touchdown on the first of those drives and a field goal on the second would have made it 41 points and cashed the Over 40.5.

Gay kicked a 43-yarder on fourth-and-20 at 2:04. Seahawks 21, Raiders 13. The Raiders +6.5 still needed the ball back, and Seattle's quarterback scrambled 15 yards on second-and-11 at 1:55 to end that idea. Three kneel-downs later, the Seahawks −6.5 had covered by 1.5, the game had 34 points, and Follow The Money's Under cashed by 6.5 at the close.

Missed at both numbers: Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Raiders, missed by 1 point at the opening Raiders +7 and missed by 1.5 points at the closing Raiders +6.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over, fell short by 9.5 points at the opening 43.5 and fell short by 6.5 points at the closing 40.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on the Seahawks, covered by 1 point at the opening Seahawks −7 and covered by 1.5 points at the closing Seahawks −6.5; Follow The Money on the Under, stayed under by 9.5 points at the opening 43.5 and stayed under by 6.5 points at the closing 40.5.

Opening line: Rams −10.5, over/under 47.5. Closing line: Rams −10, over/under 38.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Cardinals and the Over, projecting Rams 27, Cardinals 19. Final: Rams 34, Cardinals 6. The Rams won by 28, and the teams scored 40 points.

Every picker with a side had the Cardinals +9.5, and every one of them had the Over 38.5. Follow The Money skipped the side and took the Under. The over/under dropped 9 points from the open to the close, so this one was decided by which number you were holding.

Arizona led 6-3 after two Chad Ryland field goals from 49. Then Matthew Stafford hit Tyler Higbee for a 5-yard touchdown at 1:06 of the second, Kamren Kinchens intercepted Carson Beck, and Stafford found Xavier Smith for a 22-yard touchdown with 13 seconds left. Rams 17, Cardinals 6.

Blake Corum scored from 1 yard out, Wesley Bailey intercepted Beck, and Davis Allen caught a 19-yard touchdown at 5:55 of the third. Rams 31, Cardinals 6, and the Cardinals +9.5 was done. The Over 38.5 sat at 37 points.

On fourth-and-1 at the Arizona 35 late in the third, Darius Robinson jumped for a neutral zone infraction and handed the Rams a first down. Brandon McManus finished that drive with a 43-yard field goal at 14:55 of the fourth. Rams 34, Cardinals 6, 40 points. That kick cashed the Over 38.5 by 1.5 and beat Follow The Money's Under by the same 1.5.
Then the Rams kept the ball for 17 plays and 12:15, and Stafford knelt twice to end it. Anybody holding the Over at the opening 47.5 never got a sniff.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Cardinals, missed by 17.5 points at the opening Cardinals +10.5 and missed by 18 points at the closing Cardinals +10.

Split the difference: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over, fell short by 7.5 points at the opening 47.5 and went over by 1.5 points at the closing 38.5; Follow The Money on the Under, stayed under by 7.5 points at the opening 47.5 and went over by 1.5 points at the closing 38.5.
Follow The Money stayed off the side.

Opening line: Chiefs −4.5, over/under 45.5. Closing line: Chiefs −3.5, over/under 47.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Chiefs and the Under, projecting Chiefs 24, Falcons 20. Final: Chiefs 35, Falcons 13. The Chiefs won by 22, and the teams scored 48 points.

Every picker with a side had the Chiefs −3, and three of them got there late. The Cover Writer, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch had the Falcons +3.5 before Sunday's game-day line refresh and moved to Kansas City. Five pickers had the Under 47.5, and Follow The Money took the Over. In The Trenches had the Over 45.5 before the refresh and switched to the Under.

Patrick Mahomes hit Emmett Johnson for a 12-yard touchdown in the first quarter, and Jake Moody's 28-yarder got Atlanta on the board. Right before the half, a Harrison Butker field goal came off the board when Mike Ford Jr. was flagged for offside, and Mahomes threw an 18-yard touchdown to Josh Downs on the next snap. Chiefs 14, Falcons 3.

Cyrus Allen caught a 39-yard touchdown in the third, and a roughing the passer flag on Brandon Dorlus set up Johnson's second touchdown, from 6 yards, at 9:55 of the fourth. Chiefs 28, Falcons 3. The Chiefs −3 was safe. The Under had 31 points on the board and the rest of the fourth quarter to survive.

Atlanta came alive at exactly the wrong time for the Under. An offside flag on third-and-4 gave Bijan Robinson another shot, and he scored from 3 yards. A pass interference flag on Chamarri Conner set up Moody's 38-yarder at 6:45. Chiefs 28, Falcons 13, 41 points.

On third-and-1 at 4:18, Mahomes went deep to Andrew Armstrong for a 43-yard touchdown. Chiefs 35, Falcons 13, 48 points. The Under 47.5 lost by half a point, and Follow The Money's Over won by the same half point. Michael Penix Jr. got Atlanta to the Kansas City 6 on the last drive and threw incomplete on the final play, which no longer mattered to anybody holding a ticket.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Under, went over by 2.5 points at the opening 45.5 and went over by half a point at the closing 47.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Chiefs, covered by 17.5 points at the opening Chiefs −4.5 and covered by 18.5 points at the closing Chiefs −3.5; Follow The Money on the Over, went over by 2.5 points at the opening 45.5 and went over by half a point at the closing 47.5.
Follow The Money had nothing on the side.

Opening line: Texans −4.5, over/under 38.5. Closing line: Texans −3.5, over/under 41. The Cover Writer's card had the Browns and the Over, projecting Texans 23, Browns 19. Final: Texans 24, Browns 27. The Browns won by 3, and the teams scored 51 points.

The Cover Writer, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch had the Browns +4.5, and The Formula and In The Trenches had the Texans −4.5. Everybody with an over/under pick had the Over 40.5 except In The Trenches, which had the Over 39.5 before Sunday's game-day line refresh and switched to the Under 40.5.

Houston led 17-0 in the second quarter on C.J. Stroud touchdown passes to Nico Collins and Xavier Hutchinson and a 45-yarder from Ka'imi Fairbairn. Andre Szmyt hit from 49, Deshaun Watson ran in from 6 yards at 4:12 of the second, and Tyson Campbell intercepted Stroud before the half. Texans 17, Browns 10.

A face mask flag on M.J. Stewart set up KC Concepcion's 6-yard touchdown run, and Szmyt's 26-yarder with 12 seconds left in the third gave Cleveland a 20-17 lead. Szmyt missed from 54 at 11:07 of the fourth.

Then the flags took over. Emmanuel McNeil-Warren intercepted Stroud, a 37-yard pass interference call on Myles Harden wiped it out, and Stroud hit Dalton Schultz for an 11-yard touchdown at 9:17. Texans 24, Browns 20, 44 points, and the Over had cashed at every number. With Houston up 4, the Browns +4.5 was covering by half a point, the Browns at the closing +3.5 were losing by half a point, and the Texans −4.5 was losing by half a point.

Calen Bullock intercepted Watson at 5:19. Cleveland got one more chance, a 15-yard unnecessary roughness flag on Kamari Lassiter moved it into Houston territory, Harold Fannin Jr. caught a 30-yarder to the 5, and Quinshon Judkins ran in from there with 53 seconds left. Browns 27, Texans 24. Houston converted a fourth-and-10, but a holding call on Febechi Nwaiwu took it back, and the fourth-and-20 pass fell incomplete. The Browns +4.5 covered by 7.5, and the Texans −4.5 missed by the same 7.5.

Missed at both numbers: The Formula and In The Trenches on the Texans, missed by 7.5 points at the opening Texans −4.5 and missed by 6.5 points at the closing Texans −3.5; In The Trenches on the Under, went over by 12.5 points at the opening 38.5 and went over by 10 points at the closing 41.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Browns, covered by 7.5 points at the opening Browns +4.5 and covered by 6.5 points at the closing Browns +3.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and Follow The Money on the Over, went over by 12.5 points at the opening 38.5 and went over by 10 points at the closing 41.
Follow The Money took a pass on the side.

Opening line: Packers −4.5, over/under 45.5. Closing line: Packers −2.5, over/under 42.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Vikings and the Under, projecting Packers 20, Vikings 18. Final: Vikings 30, Packers 10. The Vikings won by 20, and the teams scored 40 points.
The Formula was alone on the Packers −2.5, and everybody else with a side had the Vikings +2.5. Five pickers had the Under 42.5, and Follow The Money took the Over.

Andrew Van Ginkel punched the ball loose after a short Green Bay completion in the first quarter and recovered it himself at the Green Bay 10, and Will Reichard kicked a 34-yarder. Trey Smack missed from 53. On third-and-8, a face mask flag on DeeJay Dallas pushed Minnesota back to third-and-23, and Kirk Cousins hit Myles Price for a 38-yard touchdown anyway. Harrison Smith intercepted Jordan Love in the end zone, and Aaron Jones Sr. scored from 1 yard out. Vikings 17, Packers 0 at the half.

A fumbled exchange in the third, recovered by Dallas Turner, set up Reichard's 32-yarder. Love hit J. Michael Sturdivant for a 32-yard touchdown, and Smack hit from 40 with 19 seconds left in the quarter. Vikings 20, Packers 10, 30 points.
Cousins hit Gavin Bartholomew for a 20-yard touchdown at 8:29 of the fourth, Sturdivant fumbled the kickoff, and Jake Golday recovered at the Green Bay 35. Vikings 27, Packers 10, 37 points.

Here is where the Under got its break. Minnesota got to fourth-and-goal at the 2 and kicked a 20-yard field goal at 3:56. A touchdown there makes it 44 points and beats the Under 42.5. Reichard's chip shot left it at 40, Jordan Mason ran the ball four straight times at the end, and nobody scored again. The Under cashed by 2.5 at the close, and Follow The Money's Over came up 2.5 short. The Vikings +2.5 covered by 22.5, and The Formula's Packers −2.5 missed by the same 22.5.

Missed at both numbers: The Formula on the Packers, missed by 24.5 points at the opening Packers −4.5 and missed by 22.5 points at the closing Packers −2.5; Follow The Money on the Over, fell short by 5.5 points at the opening 45.5 and fell short by 2.5 points at the closing 42.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch, Follow The Money and In The Trenches on the Vikings, covered by 24.5 points at the opening Vikings +4.5 and covered by 22.5 points at the closing Vikings +2.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Under, stayed under by 5.5 points at the opening 45.5 and stayed under by 2.5 points at the closing 42.5.

Opening line: Jaguars −2.5, over/under 45.5. Closing line: Jaguars −11, over/under 45.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Titans and the Under, projecting Jaguars 27, Titans 17. Final: Jaguars 40, Titans 23. The Jaguars won by 17, and the teams scored 63 points.

This line moved 8.5 points toward Jacksonville between the open and the close. The Cover Writer, Next Man Up and In The Trenches took the Titans +10.5, and The Formula and Letdown Watch took the Jaguars −10.5. Everybody but In The Trenches had the Under 46.5, and Follow The Money passed on both.

Trevor Lawrence hit Parker Washington for a 2-yard touchdown, and Cam Little kicked three first-half field goals, the last a 36-yarder as the half ended. Joey Slye hit from 53, and Cam Ward found Daniel Bellinger for a 2-yard touchdown. Jaguars 16, Titans 10.

Slye's 54-yarder made it 16-13. Slye then forced a fumble on the kickoff return, but Jahlani Tavai fell on it for Jacksonville, and a roughing the passer flag on John Franklin-Myers on third down kept the drive alive. Lawrence hit Brenton Strange for a 3-yard touchdown on fourth-and-2. Jaguars 23, Titans 13. Slye answered from 50. Jaguars 23, Titans 16, 39 points.

Lawrence and Josh Cameron connected for a 25-yard touchdown at 9:44 of the fourth. Jaguars 30, Titans 16, 46 points. The Under at the opening and closing 45.5 was gone, and the card's 46.5 was alive by half a point. It lasted one Tennessee drive: Tony Pollard caught a 32-yard touchdown at 8:21. Jaguars 30, Titans 23, 53 points.

Now the side was the sweat. Little's 40-yarder at 4:31 made it Jaguars 33, Titans 23, and the Titans +10.5 was covering by half a point. Pollard was stopped for a 1-yard loss on fourth-and-1 at the Tennessee 29 at 3:11, Lawrence hit Cameron for 14 yards on third-and-6, and Bhayshul Tuten ran in from 6 yards at 1:10. Jaguars 40, Titans 23. The Titans +10.5 missed by 6.5, the Jaguars −10.5 covered by 6.5, and In The Trenches' Over cashed by 16.5.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Titans, missed by 14.5 points at the opening Titans +2.5 and missed by 6 points at the closing Titans +11; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Under, went over by 17.5 points at the opening 45.5 and went over by 17.5 points at the closing 45.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Formula and Letdown Watch on the Jaguars, covered by 14.5 points at the opening Jaguars −2.5 and covered by 6 points at the closing Jaguars −11; In The Trenches on the Over, went over by 17.5 points at the opening 45.5 and went over by 17.5 points at the closing 45.5.
Follow The Money kept its money off the side and the over/under.

Opening line: Colts −6.5, over/under 47.5. Closing line: Colts −5, over/under 37.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Dolphins and the Over, projecting Colts 24, Dolphins 20. Final: Dolphins 22, Colts 24. The Colts won by 2, and the teams scored 46 points.

Three pickers changed sides here before kickoff. The Cover Writer, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches had the Colts −2.5 before Sunday's game-day line refresh and finished on the Dolphins +4.5, alongside The Formula. Next Man Up stayed with the Colts at −4.5, and Follow The Money joined it. Everybody had the Over 37.5 except Follow The Money, which took the Under. The over/under fell 10 points from the open to the close.

Zane Gonzalez missed from 47 in the first quarter. Seth McGowan scored from 4 yards out, Malik Washington threw a 34-yard touchdown pass to Jalen Tolbert, and Daniel Jones hit Laquon Treadwell for a 7-yard touchdown with 39 seconds left in the half. Colts 14, Dolphins 7.

On Miami's first snap of the second half, Justin Walley sacked Kyle McCord and forced a fumble, and Adetomiwa Adebawore recovered it in the end zone. Colts 21, Dolphins 7. Gonzalez hit from 53. Then Chris Johnson picked off Jones and went 59 yards for a touchdown, and Gonzalez missed the extra point wide left. Colts 21, Dolphins 16. Spencer Shrader's 51-yarder made it 24-16, 40 points, and the Over at the closing 37.5 was home.

McCord ran in from 3 yards at 14:56 of the fourth, and the two-point pass to Greg Dulcich fell incomplete. Colts 24, Dolphins 22, 46 points. Gonzalez then missed from 51 at 9:54. Add up the missed extra point, the failed two-point try and that 51-yarder, and the Over at the opening 47.5 lost by 1.5 on 6 points that never happened.

A Colts interception at 6:17 came off the board on an illegal contact flag on Kenneth Harris, Miami turned it over on downs at 1:41, and Jones knelt it out. The Colts won by 2. The Dolphins +4.5 covered by 2.5, so the Sunday switch paid, and the Colts −4.5 from Next Man Up and Follow The Money missed by 2.5.
Missed at both numbers: Next Man Up and Follow The Money on the Colts, missed by 4.5 points at the opening Colts −6.5 and missed by 3 points at the closing Colts −5.

Split the difference: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over, fell short by 1.5 points at the opening 47.5 and went over by 8.5 points at the closing 37.5; Follow The Money on the Under, stayed under by 1.5 points at the opening 47.5 and went over by 8.5 points at the closing 37.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Dolphins, covered by 4.5 points at the opening Dolphins +6.5 and covered by 3 points at the closing Dolphins +5.

Opening line: Saints −1.5, over/under 43.5. Closing line: Panthers −1.5, over/under 48.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Panthers and the Over, projecting Panthers 25, Saints 24. Final: Panthers 20, Saints 17. The Panthers won by 3, and the teams scored 37 points.

Four pickers had the Panthers +1.5, and Letdown Watch had the Saints −1.5. The Cover Writer, The Formula and In The Trenches had the Over 48.5, Next Man Up and Letdown Watch had the Under, and Follow The Money stayed away. The favorite flipped between the open and the close, so the same Panthers ticket was +1.5 or −1.5 depending on when it was bought.

Nobody scored in the first quarter. Devin Lloyd intercepted Tyler Shough on fourth-and-1, Ryan Fitzgerald missed from 48, and Chuba Hubbard's 12-yard touchdown came back on a holding call on Luke Fortner. Hubbard scored from 2 yards on fourth-and-goal at 6:43 of the second. Panthers 7, Saints 0 at the half, and the Over crowd was already doing math.

Alvin Kamara scored from 3 yards at 6:33 of the third, and Fitzgerald hit from 55. Panthers 10, Saints 7. A 17-yard pass interference call on Corey Thornton set up Shough's 4-yard touchdown pass to Kamara at 3:49 of the fourth. Saints 14, Panthers 10.

Hubbard scored from 1 yard at 1:49. Panthers 17, Saints 14. A face mask flag moved the Saints into range, and Charlie Smyth tied it with a 55-yarder at 0:41. At 17-17 the Panthers +1.5 was covering, and the Panthers at the closing −1.5 were losing by 1.5.

Carolina had 41 seconds. Kool-Aid McKinstry was flagged for 30 yards of pass interference, and Fitzgerald hit a 54-yarder as time ran out. Panthers 20, Saints 17. The Panthers covered by 4.5 at the card's +1.5 and by 1.5 at the closing −1.5, and Letdown Watch's Saints −1.5 missed by 4.5. The game finished with 37 points, and the Under cashed by 11.5 at the close.

Missed at both numbers: Letdown Watch on the Saints, missed by 4.5 points at the opening Saints −1.5 and missed by 1.5 points at the closing Saints +1.5; The Cover Writer, The Formula and In The Trenches on the Over, fell short by 6.5 points at the opening 43.5 and fell short by 11.5 points at the closing 48.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Panthers, covered by 4.5 points at the opening Panthers +1.5 and covered by 1.5 points at the closing Panthers −1.5; Next Man Up and Letdown Watch on the Under, stayed under by 6.5 points at the opening 43.5 and stayed under by 11.5 points at the closing 48.5.
Follow The Money passed on the side and the over/under.

Opening line: Bills −7, over/under 46.5. Closing line: Bills −8, over/under 50.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Jets and the Under, projecting Bills 28, Jets 21. Final: Bills 31, Jets 12. The Bills won by 19, and the teams scored 43 points.
Everybody but Letdown Watch had the Jets +8.5, and Letdown Watch took the Bills −8.5. All five over/under pickers had the Under 50.5, and Follow The Money stayed out.

Buffalo led 10-6 at the half. Jason Sanders kicked his third and fourth field goals of the day, from 22 and 48, around a 1-yard Josh Allen touchdown run, and the Jets were within 17-12 with 4:21 left in the third. The Jets +8.5 was comfortably alive.

It lasted 39 seconds. Allen hit DJ Moore for a 45-yard touchdown. Bills 24, Jets 12. Davison Igbinosun intercepted Cade Klubnik and fumbled it right back, and Azareye'h Thomas picked off Allen at 13:10 of the fourth.

Then the Jets drove to the Buffalo 23, where a touchdown would have pulled them within 5. Garrett Wilson caught a pass at the 19 and fumbled, Kaleb Elarms-Orr recovered at 4:59, and on the very next play James Cook III ran 74 yards for a touchdown. Bills 31, Jets 12, 43 points. The Jets +8.5 missed by 10.5, and Letdown Watch's Bills −8.5 covered by the same 10.5.

The Under still had one scare left. The Jets got to the Buffalo 29 and threw incomplete on fourth-and-11 at 1:54, and Kyle Allen knelt twice. A Jets touchdown there makes it 50 points, still half a point under the closing 50.5 but over the opening 46.5. The Under cashed by 3.5 at the open and 7.5 at the close.
Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Jets, missed by 12 points at the opening Jets +7 and missed by 11 points at the closing Jets +8.

Called it at both numbers: Letdown Watch on the Bills, covered by 12 points at the opening Bills −7 and covered by 11 points at the closing Bills −8; The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Under, stayed under by 3.5 points at the opening 46.5 and stayed under by 7.5 points at the closing 50.5.
Follow The Money stayed off the side and the over/under.

Opening line: Lions −1.5, over/under 48.5. Closing line: Lions −2.5, over/under 50.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Patriots and the Over, projecting Patriots 26, Lions 25. Final: Patriots 10, Lions 35. The Lions won by 25, and the teams scored 45 points.

All five pickers with a side had the Patriots +2.5. Before Sunday's game-day line refresh, The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches all had the Under 51.5. The refresh moved The Cover Writer, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches to the Over 50.5. The Formula and Next Man Up stayed on the Under 50.5, and Follow The Money joined them at Under 50.

Drake Maye moved New England to the Detroit 7 on the opening drive, then took a third-down sack from Aidan Hutchinson at 9:43 and did not take another snap. Andy Borregales kicked a 33-yarder, and Tommy DeVito played the rest of the way.

Jared Goff hit Amon-Ra St. Brown for a 56-yard touchdown, Isaac TeSlaa caught a 12-yard touchdown, and Jahmyr Gibbs ran 5 yards for another. Kevin Byard intercepted Goff in the end zone with 12 seconds left in the half, with Detroit sitting at the New England 3. Lions 21, Patriots 3. The Patriots +2.5 was already down 18.

St. Brown's 28-yard touchdown made it 28-3 at 8:16 of the third, 31 points. A 20-yard touchdown pass to Lan Larison came back on offensive pass interference by Efton Chism III, a pass interference flag on Nick Whiteside gave New England new life, and DeVito hit Larison for a 10-yard touchdown at 12:40 of the fourth. Lions 28, Patriots 10, 38 points.

Gibbs ran 28 yards for a touchdown at 8:56. Lions 35, Patriots 10, 45 points. That was the last score. An offensive pass interference flag on TeSlaa wiped out a 15-yard gain on the next Detroit drive, and Joshua Dobbs knelt three times to finish it. The Over 50.5 fell 5.5 short, and the Under 51.5 that three of them traded away on Sunday would have cashed by 6.5.

Missed at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Patriots, missed by 23.5 points at the opening Patriots +1.5 and missed by 22.5 points at the closing Patriots +2.5; The Cover Writer, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over, fell short by 3.5 points at the opening 48.5 and fell short by 5.5 points at the closing 50.5.
Called it at both numbers: The Formula, Next Man Up and Follow The Money on the Under, stayed under by 3.5 points at the opening 48.5 and stayed under by 5.5 points at the closing 50.5.
Follow The Money kept its money off the side.

Opening line: Giants −1.5, over/under 47.5. Closing line: Giants −1.5, over/under 40.5. The Cover Writer's card had the Commanders and the Over, projecting Giants 23, Commanders 22. Final: Commanders 24, Giants 21. The Commanders won by 3, and the teams scored 45 points.

The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches had the Commanders +2.5, and Letdown Watch had the Giants −2.5. Five pickers had the Over 41.5, and Follow The Money took the Under. The over/under fell 7 points from the open to the close, which made the Over a different bet depending on the day it was placed.

Dominic Zvada missed a 33-yarder for the Giants in the first quarter. Drew Stevens hit from 46, a pass interference flag on Jeremy Reaves set up Cam Skattebo's 1-yard touchdown, and Jayden Daniels hit Ben Sinnott for a 1-yard touchdown with 5 seconds left in the half. Commanders 10, Giants 7.

Skattebo ran 13 yards for a touchdown in the third, and Daniels answered with a 31-yard touchdown pass to Antonio Williams. Commanders 17, Giants 14. Reaves recovered a Malik Nabers fumble at the Washington 20. Isaiah Likely caught a 66-yard touchdown at 8:13 of the fourth. Giants 21, Commanders 17, 38 points.

Washington's next two drives ended in Daniels interceptions, by Jevon Holland at the Giants' 2 and by Ar'Darius Washington on fourth-and-2 at 2:19. Letdown Watch's Giants −2.5 was covering by 1.5, the Commanders +2.5 was losing by 1.5, and Follow The Money's Under 41.5 was alive by 3.5.

Then Jordan Stout punted 12 yards out of bounds at 1:54. Deonte Banks was flagged for 33 yards of pass interference, and Daniels hit Stefon Diggs for a 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds left. Commanders 24, Giants 21, 45 points. Rasul Douglas picked off J.J. McCarthy at the Washington 11, and Daniels knelt it out. The Commanders +2.5 covered by 5.5, Letdown Watch's Giants −2.5 missed by 5.5, and the Over cashed by 4.5 at the close but fell 2.5 short of the opening 47.5.
Missed at both numbers: Letdown Watch on the Giants, missed by 4.5 points at the opening Giants −1.5 and missed by 4.5 points at the closing Giants −1.5.

Split the difference: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up, Letdown Watch and In The Trenches on the Over, fell short by 2.5 points at the opening 47.5 and went over by 4.5 points at the closing 40.5; Follow The Money on the Under, stayed under by 2.5 points at the opening 47.5 and went over by 4.5 points at the closing 40.5.

Called it at both numbers: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Commanders, covered by 4.5 points at the opening Commanders +1.5 and covered by 4.5 points at the closing Commanders +1.5.
Follow The Money sat out the side.

hits.heading: Part 1, continued: The week's W-L and smack talk

paragraphs: The Cover Writer missed 15 times and hit 11 times at the opening lines, and missed 12 times and hit 14 times at the closing lines, with no pushes and Monday night still to come.

The Cover Writer is 8-5 against the spread at both numbers, and 3-10 on the over/under at the open and 6-7 at the close. Sunday's line refresh was kind on the side and cruel on the over/under. Leaving the Falcons for the Chiefs cashed, and leaving the Colts for the Dolphins cashed. Leaving the Under 51.5 in Munich for the Over 50.5 turned a winner into a loser in a 45-point game, and that one is going to come up at every meeting until Thanksgiving. Tonight the card has the Chargers +4.5 and the Over 38.5.

The Formula is 8-5 against the spread at both numbers, and 4-9 on the over/under at the open and 7-6 at the close. The Formula was alone on the Bengals on Sunday night and alone on the Packers in Green Bay. One of those was a 20-point win, and the other was a 20-point loss, so The Formula would like everybody to remember Sunday night. Tonight it breaks from the card again with the Ravens −4.5 and the Over.

Next Man Up is 5-8 against the spread at both numbers, and 5-8 on the over/under at the open and 8-5 at the close. Next Man Up had the Seahawks −3.5 and the Under 43.5 in the Raiders game before Sunday's refresh, switched to the Raiders +6.5 and the Over 40.5, and lost both. The original pair would have cashed both. Tonight it has the Chargers +4.5 and the Over.

Letdown Watch is 8-5 against the spread at both numbers, and 4-9 on the over/under at the open and 7-6 at the close. Letdown Watch was the only Giants backer on Thursday night and lost it on a Stefon Diggs touchdown with 57 seconds left, then went 8-4 on the side the rest of the week. Since opening-line grading began in Week 8, Letdown Watch is 24-18 against the spread at the open, the best mark in the room, and it will bring that up before anyone asks. Tonight it has the Ravens −4.5 and the Over.

Follow The Money is 2-1 against the spread at both numbers, and 8-1 on the over/under at the open and 5-4 at the close. Follow The Money only showed up on three sides and cashed two of them, the Seahawks and the Vikings. The one over/under that lost at both numbers was the Over in Green Bay, where Minnesota kicked a field goal on fourth-and-goal at the 2 instead of scoring a touchdown, which Follow The Money is taking personally. Tonight it has the Chargers +4.5 and nothing on the over/under.

In The Trenches is 6-7 against the spread at both numbers, and 4-9 on the over/under at the open and 7-6 at the close. In The Trenches changed its over/under on five games in Sunday's refresh: the Under in Munich, the Over in Atlanta, the Over in Cleveland, the Under against the Raiders and the Over in Cincinnati. The call it walked away from would have cashed all five times, and the new call lost all five times. It also left the Seahawks −3.5 for the Raiders +6.5, which lost too. The Over in Dallas, the one it never touched, cashed by 30.5. Tonight it has the Chargers +4.5 and the Over 38.5, and the room would like those to stay put.

look_ahead.heading: Part 2: Looking forward

paragraphs: Kickoff is 8:15 PM ET tonight on ESPN at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore. The Chargers come in 0-8, 0-4 on the road, and lost to the Texans 44-22 last time out. The Ravens are 4-5, 1-3 at home, and lost to the Jaguars 33-10 last time out. The Chargers are still looking for their first win.

Today's number: DraftKings has the Ravens −4.5 with the over/under at 38.5 as of 2:52 AM ET Monday, and the Action Network consensus matches it. The card was built on that same number, so tonight's picks are graded right where they were made.

The card has the Chargers +4.5 and the Over 38.5, projecting Ravens 23, Chargers 19. The Formula has the Ravens −4.5 and the Over, projecting Ravens 25, Chargers 19. Next Man Up has the Chargers +4.5 and the Over, projecting Ravens 22, Chargers 21. Letdown Watch has the Ravens −4.5 and the Over, projecting Ravens 25, Chargers 18. Follow The Money has the Chargers +4.5 and no over/under pick. In The Trenches has the Chargers +4.5 and the Over, projecting Ravens 21, Chargers 18.

Four of the six cards are taking the points with the winless Chargers, two are laying them with Baltimore, and every over/under pick on the board is the Over. A Ravens win by 5 or more cashes The Formula and Letdown Watch on the side, and anything less pays the other four. The Over needs 39 points, and Baltimore has to find its share of them without Lamar Jackson.

ESPN lists Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley on injured reserve, and Next Man Up's card names Jacoby Brissett as the expected Ravens starter. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins is out for Baltimore. The Chargers are without wide receiver Ladd McConkey, guard Branson Taylor and safety Kendall Williamson, and tackle Trey Pipkins III is on injured reserve. Jackson has 967 passing yards and 6 touchdowns, Derrick Henry has 689 rushing yards and 8 touchdowns, Zay Flowers has 614 receiving yards, and Mike Green has 3.5 sacks. Justin Herbert has thrown for 1,591 yards with 6 touchdowns and 11 interceptions, Omarion Hampton has 369 rushing yards, and Khalil Mack has 3 sacks.
